reconstructed.context: In September 2020 the repository was created as a monorepo using Yarn workspaces. The team needed a set of libraries for testing, validation, server runtime, and the web front‑end, as well as tooling for building and linting the codebase.

Future changes to the stack would need to migrate existing code and scripts that depend on these packages.
reconstructed.inference: The decision appears to be driven by a desire for a full‑stack TypeScript monorepo with a clear separation of concerns: React/Next for the UI, Node.js with nodemon for the server, and mature testing/validation tools (chai, jest, joi). The inclusion of ts-node and TypeScript suggests the team wanted static typing across the codebase. This inference is based on the combination of packages introduced in the initial commit.

real.title: Expose command line interface
real.excerpt: Date: 2018-09-02 ## Status Accepted ## Context We want to maximise the usability of adr-viewer whilst maintaining flexibility in future for other output formats, e.g. a live webserver. ## Decision The entry point for this project will be a command-line utility called `adr-viewer`. We will use the python [click](http://click.pocoo.org/5/) library to provide command-line options and documentation. ## Consequences Click will be added as a dependency, and further improvements should consider the user experience of the command-line interface.

reconstructed.title: Adopt click for CLI interface
reconstructed.context: The project needed a command‑line interface to generate HTML from ADR files. The developers added a new dependency and rewrote the entry point to use a library that provides option parsing and help generation. The commit message explicitly mentions using click for the CLI. Documentation later shows that the help output displays default values, a feature of click.
reconstructed.decision: The project decided to use the click library as the implementation of its command‑line interface.
reconstructed.consequences: The code now imports click and defines the main command with @click.command and @click.option decorators. The requirements.txt and setup.py were updated to include click as a runtime dependency. Subsequent commits reference the new CLI options (e.g., showing defaults in help), indicating that other parts of the codebase rely on click's API. Adding this dependency also introduces an external package that must be maintained and bundled with the project.
reconstructed.inference: Based on the commit message "Using click library for cli interface" and the code changes that replace a manual argument handling approach with click decorators, we infer that the developers chose click to obtain a structured, declarative CLI with built‑in help and default handling, reducing boilerplate and improving usability.

real.title: Loader Multi-Worker Pipeline
real.excerpt: ## Status Accepted ## Context The Plex loader previously executed ingestion, enrichment, and Qdrant writes sequentially. Each phase waited for the previous phase to finish, so TMDb and IMDb lookups, embedding generation, and upsert requests could not overlap. Large libraries therefore spent most of their time idle while waiting on network latency, and any failure in a downstream phase required rerunning the entire load. Stakeholders asked for the "loader multi worker rearchitecture plan" to overlap these phases, provide better fault isolation, and expose concurrency controls. The development team added a new dev‑dependency on the `coverage[toml]` package and extended the test suite to cover edge cases in loader and server components. The change also bumped the project version to reflect the new release.
reconstructed.decision: The repository adopted the `coverage` package as a development dependency and updated tests to enable local coverage reporting.
reconstructed.consequences: Subsequent commits continue to reference the updated version number and retain the `coverage` entry in the dependency manifest, indicating the dependency remains in use. The expanded test suite provides more thorough verification of loader retry logic and server request handling, supporting the goal of >96% coverage. Adding the dependency also required updating the Docker dependency manifest to keep version metadata in sync.
reconstructed.inference: The decision to adopt `coverage` appears driven by a stated requirement to achieve test coverage above 96% (as noted in PR #72). Adding the dependency enabled the team to run `coverage run -m pytest` locally and verify the new tests increased coverage. The version bump and Docker manifest updates were necessary to keep all packaging metadata consistent after the new dependency was introduced.
